intended_object: The radial contraction of a tubular neighborhood: the homotopy H : [0,1] × U → U, H(t,(x,v)) = (x, t·v), which deforms the fiberwise star-shaped domain U onto the zero section. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the lemmas right after it (value at t=1 is the identity, value at t=0 is on the zero section, continuity).
explanation: The body sends (t, ⟨x, v⟩) to ⟨x, t • v⟩, which is exactly the standard radial deformation. The proof that the image stays in U uses the structure's fiberwise star-convexity at 0, which says precisely that t·v stays in the fiber slice of U for t ∈ [0,1]. So the map is a well-defined self-map of U. The lemmas after it confirm the expected behaviour: it is the identity at t=1, lands on the zero section at t=0, and is continuous. Using real scalars is the natural setting for tubular neighborhoods, and the fiber setting (any family of real modules over the total space) is already general, so the definition is not too narrow. I did not search Mathlib, but I know of no counterpart, since Mathlib has no theory of tubular neighborhoods.
